incidents.victim: Organizations globally using Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway
incidents.vector: Unauthenticated remote code execution via CVE-2026-88771 (improper input validation) and memory overflow via CVE-2026-88772; both zero-days exploited in the wild before patches were available; mass exploitation observed within hours of disclosure
incidents.impact: Active exploitation confirmed in Australia, UK, and globally; 50,000+ internet-exposed instances identified; attackers gain arbitrary command execution on network edge devices; exploitation window began at least September 4

incidents.victim: Water utility, telecom, regional government, and university in Spain and Portugal
incidents.vector: SharePoint ToolShell exploit chain for initial access; DLL sideloading and Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver (BYOVD) for persistence and defense bypass; VS Code remote tunneling for covert C2; ransomware distributed across victim networks via Active Directory SYSVOL
incidents.impact: Ransomware deployed across multiple critical infrastructure and government sectors in Spain and Portugal; attack attributed to a China-nexus group; ongoing incident response in affected organizations

incidents.victim: AI policy experts at US think tanks, universities, and law firms
incidents.vector: Spear-phishing impersonating former White House AI policy official Lynne Parker and economist Heidi Crebo-Rediker; adversary-in-the-middle attacks using Frameless BitB phishing tool; fake Microsoft OneDrive sign-in pages capturing credentials and active browser sessions
incidents.impact: Cloud account credentials and session tokens targeted from AI policy experts; campaign focused on AI export controls, semiconductor supply chains, and military AI development; a February 2026 campaign also impersonated a senior Anthropic employee to target defense AI policy analysts

incidents.victim: Organizations using Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager
incidents.vector: API authentication bypass via URI encoding in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager; unauthenticated attackers can access the management API by URI-encoding parts of the request URL to bypass authentication checks; zero-day with patch now available
incidents.impact: Exploitation confirmed in the wild before patch release; unauthenticated API access to SD-WAN management infrastructure; organizations urged to investigate for prior compromise before applying patch

incidents.victim: KillSec ransomware victims — 500+ organizations globally
incidents.vector: Ransomware-as-a-service platform with $250 entry fee and 88% affiliate payout; exploitation of unpatched server and cloud storage vulnerabilities for initial access; double-extortion scheme combining data theft with ransomware deployment
incidents.impact: 500+ confirmed victims including 70+ government organizations across the globe; Operation KillSwitch resulted in 3 arrests including the alleged 16-year-old Romanian ringleader; 110TB of stolen data secured; KillSec infrastructure and dark web leak site seized; US extradition request filed for Dutch national Fouad Eltibrizi

incidents.victim: NGOs, think tanks, journalists, and Ukraine-linked organizations
incidents.vector: New RedFlick phishing technique with CosmicPulse Python backdoor; 13 large-scale campaigns since January 2026; widened from targeted spear-phishing to mass campaigns; iOS devices targeted via DarkSword exploit kit deployed through compromised websites
incidents.impact: Ongoing compromise of civil society organizations, media outlets, and Ukraine-linked entities; Apple iOS device exploitation expanded targeting surface; campaign intensity and scale increased significantly compared to prior years

incidents.victim: Ukrainian military personnel and government officials
incidents.vector: DarkSword iOS exploit kit deployed via watering-hole attacks on compromised Ukrainian news and government websites; exploits Safari and iOS vulnerabilities with zero or minimal user interaction; CamelSpy and BTMOB malware families used against Android devices via fake Ukrainian service apps
incidents.impact: Military communications, credentials, contacts, and call histories stolen from iPhones and Android devices; DarkSword operates as a hit-and-run tool, extracting data in minutes and removing itself; Ukraine's CERT recorded 3,137 cyber incidents in first half of 2026

incidents.victim: Air Traffic and Navigation Services (ATNS) — South Africa
incidents.vector: Ransomware-linked malware deployed in OT network serving weather services for air traffic controllers at Port Elizabeth Airport; data exfiltrated to Chinese IP addresses; possible insider collaboration under investigation at Maputo Airport
incidents.impact: OT network disrupted at Port Elizabeth Airport affecting weather services critical to air traffic control; ATNS manages 6% of global airspace; investigation ongoing with potential insider threat dimension; attack could have crippled both domestic and international air travel

incidents.victim: US financial institutions — multiple unnamed
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — financial fraud (Tren de Aragua)
incidents.vector: ATM jackpotting malware deployed directly in US bank ATMs; malware forced ATMs to dispense cash on demand; 1,500+ attacks executed across US financial institutions
incidents.impact: $40.73 million stolen from US financial institutions; OFAC sanctioned 10 individuals and entities in the Venezuelan Tren de Aragua criminal network responsible for the campaign

incidents.victim: US Defense Manpower Data Center (Pentagon — DMDC)
incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to a file-sharing server maintained by the Pentagon's Defense Manpower Data Center; access persisted undetected for approximately nine months before discovery
incidents.impact: 3.1 million current and former US military personnel records exposed — 2.8 million living individuals and 294,000 deceased service members; data includes personally identifiable information of active duty and veteran personnel

incidents.victim: OpenAI
incidents.attacker: China — suspected state-linked IP theft operation
incidents.vector: Novel encryption bypass — attackers copied encrypted reasoning data from one conversation and used a separate conversation to instruct the model to decrypt and transcribe it; coordinated campaign using 15,000 accounts between July 1 and July 28
incidents.impact: OpenAI model reasoning capabilities potentially extracted at scale; attack blocked July 28; vulnerability details shared with Frontier Model Forum; individuals linked to Chinese AI company Moonshot AI identified as a core cluster; similar vulnerability exists in other AI models

incidents.victim: SpetsVuzAvtomatika — Russian SVR cyber R&D center
incidents.vector: Unauthorized access and data exfiltration from internal systems of the Russian SVR cyber research and development center previously sanctioned by the US Treasury
incidents.impact: Internal documents leaked exposing Russian offensive cyber tools including capabilities for target discovery, network scanning, credential theft, and data exfiltration; SpetsVuzAvtomatika was sanctioned by US Treasury in May 2021 for developing hacking tools for Russia's SVR

incidents.victim: Fakturownia — Polish invoicing platform (600,000 businesses)
incidents.vector: Vulnerability exploited in Fakturownia's systems; unauthorized server access by threat actor 'Fingerprint'; same group also breached Polish healthcare platforms MyDr (18.8 million individuals) and Medyc
incidents.impact: Password hashes, bank account information, authentication and integration tokens, and historical invoices for up to 600,000 businesses potentially exposed; 6TB of data claimed stolen; Polish national KSeF e-invoicing system confirmed unaffected

incidents.victim: FBI (apply.fbijobs.gov) and dozens of organizations
incidents.vector: Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day CVE-2026-35273 exploited at mass scale; FBI's job application portal was among dozens of confirmed victims spanning higher education, tech, healthcare, agriculture, transport, and government
incidents.impact: 5,000+ FBI officials' SSNs, job titles, and psychiatric and medical records stolen; FBI confirmed the breach; ShinyHunters suspect Pepijn Van der Stap arrested in the Netherlands September 16; broader exploitation of CVE-2026-35273 hit numerous organizations across sectors

incidents.victim: Arizona courts system
incidents.vector: Cyberattack on Arizona courts infrastructure; backup court files accessed and copied; personal data of Arizona residents exfiltrated
incidents.impact: Backup court files compromised; personal data of an unspecified number of Arizonans stolen; most stolen files are public court records; Arizona Supreme Court disclosed the breach

incidents.victim: Bitget cryptocurrency exchange
incidents.vector: Zero-day exploit in a third-party security product used by the exchange; valid admin credentials extracted from the compromised device; pivot to internal network; fraudulent withdrawal commands injected; attack tracks deleted after theft to hinder forensic investigation
incidents.impact: $388 million in cryptocurrency assets stolen; one of the largest crypto exchange thefts of 2026; investigation ongoing

incidents.victim: Belnet — Belgian government internet provider
incidents.vector: Zero-day vulnerability exploited in Belnet's systems; email inboxes of Belnet itself and at least one government customer exfiltrated over a two-month window
incidents.impact: Emails stolen from July 22 to September 25; Belnet serves the Belgian government, educational institutions, and science and research centers; breach investigated with national authorities

incidents.victim: IT professionals worldwide — 30,000+ individuals
incidents.vector: Fake job interview campaigns targeting software developers and IT freelancers; malicious NPM packages (BeaverTail, InvisibleFerret, OtterCookie, OtterCandy, StoatWaffle) delivered during fake technical interviews; remote access trojans establish persistence; laptop farms used in Japan, US, and Europe to obfuscate operations
incidents.impact: 30,000+ devices infected across 100+ countries; 7,000+ cryptocurrency wallets drained; $10.71 million transferred to North Korea; laptop farm dismantled in Japan; joint advisory from FBI, Japan NPA, Australia ACSC, and Germany BfV/BND

incidents.victim: Multiple organizations across multiple sectors and regions
incidents.vector: Unauthenticated OS command injection in Zimbra Collaboration Suite via the SNMP path (CVE-2026-73570); attackers deployed JSP webshells and reverse shells, then escalated privileges via PAM sudo abuse
incidents.impact: Zimbra service credentials stolen including authentication pre-keys (zimbraPreAuthKey, zimbraAuthTokenKey); lateral movement via SSH cluster trust relationships; multiple organizations compromised between July 20 and August 13 across industries and regions

incidents.victim: Government and policy organizations across Taiwan, India, Philippines, Cambodia, Pakistan, Thailand, Myanmar, and Syria
incidents.vector: Spear-phishing with Cloudflare-delivered payloads and decoy documents; Rust-compiled Antino backdoor for reconnaissance, file transfer, and persistent access; command-and-control via Microsoft 365 Graph API, Outlook, and OneDrive used as dead drops to blend with legitimate traffic
incidents.impact: Approximately 350 endpoints compromised across 16 affected environments in 8 countries; campaign ran September 2025 to July 2026; focused on intelligence collection from government, think tank, and civil society policy organizations across Asia
